svg.title: Drama & exam writing
svg.desc: What an audience knows: Soliloquy: private thoughts. Aside: concealed from other characters. Dramatic irony: audience knows what a character does not. Track contrasts between public behaviour and private speech, rather than treating the play as a novel. How the action is staged: Duncan’s murder is offstage: anticipation and aftermath dominate. Macduff’s family faces violence onstage. Knocking interrupts the murder aftermath. Banquet shifts from ceremony to chaos. Explain why the order and staging matter. Sound, form & imagery: Much speech is blank verse; rhythmic patterns can vary. Witches’ rhyme can sound ritual-like. Lady Macbeth’s fragmented sleepwalking prose contrasts with earlier control. Blood, sleep, darkness and clothing develop repeated ideas; explain effects, not just technique names. 15-mark extract: About 20 minutes. Give a clear overview, then follow changes across the printed passage. Short evidence → precise word/action analysis → meaning → possible audience response. Keep focus on this passage; avoid retelling the whole play. 25-mark essay: About 40 minutes. 20 literary marks + 5 for writing accuracy. Plan a clear answer and three/four developing moments. Link beginning, middle and end; show how Shakespeare presents the idea. Use connected paragraphs and accurate quotation or clear event references. Flexible evidence: “Vaulting ambition”: excess and judgement. “Fruitless crown”: insecurity. “Little water” → “damned spot”: reversal and guilt. “Feel it as a man”: grief and courage. “Walking shadow”: emptiness. Explain evidence in its moment, then link it to the argument.
